SMTO-SKL-0022 — SMTO couldn't set up how this event repeats

GUID: b8c84e3e-4d94-51ec-9dac-bf23892eca24
Slug: google-calendar-recurrence-invalid
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-calendar

What happened

  • The repeat pattern for this event wasn't one SMTO can use, or it was being changed on a single date instead of the whole series. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Describe the repeat as daily, weekly on chosen weekdays, monthly on a date or a day like "second Tuesday", or yearly on a date. Don't combine a date and a weekday for monthly. SMTO supports these patterns, and each one accepts only certain details.
  2. Say how it ends with either a number of times or a last date, not both. The last date can't be before the first event. Having both endings, or an end before the start, makes the pattern contradict itself.
  3. For a repeating event at a set time, include the time zone, for example "9 am London time". Google needs the time zone to place every repeat correctly across daylight saving changes.
  4. To change how often an event repeats, ask SMTO to change the whole series, not one date in it. A single date in a series can't have its own repeat pattern.

What success looks like

  • The event repeats on the days you expect in Google Calendar.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the repeat pattern you wanted, to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Calendar recurrence object failed its schema or compile checks (unsupported field mix, both count and until, until before start, invalid date, timed series without an IANA timeZone) or a recurrence change targeted a recurring instance instead of the series master.

What this means

  • The recurrence object fails its supported schema/time constraints, or recurrence changes target a recurring instance instead of the master. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • The recurrence object fails its supported schema/time constraints, or recurrence changes target a recurring instance instead of the master.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect frequency, ending rule, timezone and recurringEventId.

How to fix it

  • Supply a structured daily, weekly, monthly or yearly rule with valid fields and at most one of count or until (until not before the start date). Timed series need an IANA timeZone on start and end. Change recurrence on the series master event ID, not an instance.
  • Supply a structured daily, weekly, monthly or yearly rule with valid fields and at most one count or until ending. Timed series need an IANA timezone. Change recurrence on the master, not an instance.

Retry and execution caution

  • Supply a structured daily, weekly, monthly or yearly rule with valid fields and at most one count or until ending. Timed series need an IANA timezone. Change recurrence on the master, not an instance.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported recurrence is applied deliberately to the exact series master.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials or private Calendar content in diagnostics.
  • Do not blindly repeat writes after uncertain provider effects.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
